text: Afternoon. Six metres under the arena, the roar of the crowd becomes a dull rumble.
This is the hypogeum. A maze of tunnels beneath the sand, lit only by flames.
In its finished form, it would hide dozens of lifts and trapdoors, all worked by hand.
The air is hot. It smells of smoke, sweat, and animals.
Because behind these bars… something is breathing.
A lion. Shipped across the sea from North Africa.
Workers lean on a wooden winch. And the cage begins to rise.
Above you, a trapdoor opens. Daylight pours in. And fifty thousand people roar at once.
The cage is gone. Up into the arena.
And then, high above your head, the sound of the crowd changes.
It is not cheering anymore. It is panic.
